agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider closing road portions at 722 Gore Avenue for a new park
agenda_briefs.summary: Vancouver Council will vote on November 17, 2026 on a resolution to close, stop-up and raise title to a 0.286-hectare portion of road at 722 Gore Avenue (Block 121, District Lot 196, Plan 13098, dedicated in 1968) and designate it permanent public park under section 488(5)(a) of the Vancouver Charter. The closure follows Reference Plan EPP155773 prepared by Elliot Perley, B.C.L.S., completed September 29, 2026. The motion is subject to Council first approving Report 4. Requests to speak must be received before 5 pm on November 16, 2026.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Submit a request to speak to Council at vancouver.ca/speak-to-council before 5 pm on November 16, 2026 if you want to address the road closure.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider rezoning 1125 West 10th Avenue to CD-1
agenda_briefs.summary: Vancouver Council will consider a bylaw that would change the zoning of 1125 West 10th Avenue to CD-1. CD-1 is a site-specific zone, meaning Council writes rules for that one property instead of using the citywide rules. The change would allow a different kind of building or use than the current zoning permits. Several councillors must first review the meeting record before they can vote on it. If approved, the new rules would apply only to this address.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the Council vote on this rezoning — if you own or lease nearby property, check how the new CD-1 rules could affect your site.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider housing agreement bylaw for 1081 West 16th Avenue
agenda_briefs.summary: Vancouver Council will consider a bylaw to enact a Housing Agreement for 1081 West 16th Avenue. A Housing Agreement is a legal deal between the city and a property owner that locks in rules for a building — such as who can live there, rental terms, or affordability levels — and it stays with the land even if the property is sold. If approved, this bylaw would make that agreement official for this site. The agenda item does not yet spell out the specific terms, so owners and neighbours should watch for the details before the vote.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision and the agreement's terms if you own or operate property near 1081 West 16th Avenue.

agenda_briefs.summary: Vancouver Council will consider a bylaw that would repeal By-law No. 14723, which authorized a housing agreement for 4975-4997 Joyce Street. A housing agreement is a legal deal between the city and a property owner that sets rules for a housing project, such as who can live there and for how long. If Council approves the repeal, that agreement would no longer be in force. The agenda item does not explain why the repeal is proposed or what would replace the agreement, so owners and tenants connected to this site should watch for details before the vote.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to receive 2026 Local General Election results report
agenda_briefs.summary: Vancouver Council will receive the Chief Election Officer's report confirming the 2026 election results, as required by section 120 of the Vancouver Charter. Voters also approved three capital borrowing questions allowing Council to borrow $292 million for transportation and technology, $438 million for community facilities, and $60 million for parks and civic facilities between January 1, 2027 and December 31, 2030. Turnout was 43.4%, with 209,711 of 483,324 registered voters casting ballots.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider consultation rules for rezoning that amends Vancouver Official Development Plan
agenda_briefs.summary: Vancouver Council will consider a report on required consultation for rezoning applications that would amend the city's Official Development Plan (ODP) — the high-level plan that sets the broad direction for growth and land use in parts of the city. The report names specific sites (including 3410-3436 Kingsway, 5680 Oak St, and 8029-8225 Oak St) where proposed heights or uses conflict with current land-use designations, and recommends consultation with the Musqueam Indian Band, Squamish Nation, Tsleil-Waututh Nation, Vancouver School Board and Conseil scolaire francophone. Council has not yet made a decision, so the current rules still apply for now.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the Council decision on Nov 17 and any new consultation steps if you plan a rezoning that changes the Official Development Plan.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Yaletown BIA expansion up for Council consideration in 2027
agenda_briefs.summary: Vancouver Council will consider expanding the Yaletown BIA to include seven commercial properties on Marinaside Crescent (folios 159-607-88-0363 to -0369, addresses 1079–1097), occupied by a bakery and café, a pet food retailer, and a veterinary clinic. The BIA's existing term (April 2024–March 2029) and levy ceiling stay unchanged. If approved, the City will notify affected owners and businesses, forward the request to a Court of Revision hearing, and report back in February 2027. Council cannot approve the expansion if most property owners oppose it and they represent more than half the area's assessed property value.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Check whether your property or business is at 1079–1097 Marinaside Crescent and watch for the City's notification and Court of Revision hearing.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider closing and turning 722 Gore Avenue into a permanent park
agenda_briefs.summary: Vancouver Council will consider a proposal to close and stop-up 722 Gore Avenue — meaning the street or lane there would be legally shut to traffic — and to raise title, which is the step that clears the way to fold that land into the city's property records. The proposal would also give the site a permanent park designation, so the land would be set aside as park space for good. The report is on the agenda but no decision has been made yet. Owners nearby should watch for possible changes to access, parking, or loading on the block.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider Business Licence Hearing Panel assignments for late 2026
agenda_briefs.summary: Vancouver Council will consider delegating business licence hearings and appeals under the Vancouver Charter to three-member Council panels on four dates: November 24 and 25, and December 8 and 9, 2026, all at 9:30 am. Each panel has a designated chair and an alternate; if a member cannot attend, the remaining two councillors plus the alternate decide. The panels hear cases where a licence is refused, suspended, or has conditions attached.
agenda_briefs.action_required: If you have a licence hearing on one of the four scheduled dates, note the panel members and alternate assigned to your date.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider annual update to Vancouver Heritage Register
agenda_briefs.summary: Council will vote on November 17, 2026 to add 8 properties to the Heritage Register and remove 13, plus 54 address changes and 5 appendix changes, bringing the register to 2,261 listings as of October 31, 2026. Additions require the owner's written consent and Heritage Commission endorsement. Deletions include buildings demolished or moved off-site, such as the Murphy House (demolished 2025) and Raymar Block (demolished 2021).
agenda_briefs.action_required: Check Appendix A to see if your property is among the 8 additions, 13 deletions, or 54 address changes.

agenda_briefs.title: Up for approval: Vancouver Community Sport Event Grants, Fall 2026 intake
agenda_briefs.summary: Vancouver Council will consider approving 21 Fall 2026 Community Sport Event Grants totalling $101,050, plus a $5,000 grant to Volleyball BC for the 2026 Vancouver Open (July 10–12, 2026) that was left off the April 14 report due to a staff error — $106,050 in total from the $244,000 program budget. Grants go to non-profit sport organizations; recipients that aren't registered charities must be deemed by Council to contribute to the city's culture, health or welfare. No legal rights are created until grant agreement letters are signed.
agenda_briefs.action_required: If you run a non-profit sport event in Vancouver, check the City's grant page for the next intake and confirm your charity status before applying.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider changes to 2026 Vancouver Council meeting schedule
agenda_briefs.summary: Vancouver Council will consider cancelling the two Meeting Reserves scheduled for December 21 and 22, 2026 at 9:30 am, to align with the Vancouver School Board's December 21–31 winter break. Council can cancel or change meeting dates under Section 2.7 of the Procedure By-law. Meeting Reserves are held in case regular meetings run long, so cancelling them removes backup dates for decisions on licences, permits, bylaws and rezoning in that week.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Check whether any licence, permit or rezoning matter you have is tied to the December 21–22, 2026 Meeting Reserves before Council votes.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider appointments to committees, boards and UNDRIP Task Force
agenda_briefs.summary: Vancouver Council will consider a motion to fill its seats on Council committees, boards, statutory committees, non-profit societies, and the UNDRIP Task Force. The agenda item is a memorandum on Council appointments. UNDRIP refers to the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples. The item does not name specific groups or appointees, so it is unclear which bodies will change. No new rules for businesses are proposed in this item. Watch for the outcome if your business works with a City committee, board, or society.
